hints: Focus on what type of reaction each set of conditions favours, substitution to add a group or elimination to remove HBr.
Remember that aqueous NaOH gives an alcohol, cyanide adds a carbon, but hot concentrated ethanolic NaOH removes HBr to form an alkene.
Compare the Mr values of ethanol (46), propanenitrile (55), propan-2-ol (60) and propene (42) to spot which is the smallest.
walkthrough:
**Sort substitution versus elimination**

Think like this: aqueous hydroxide means OH replaces Br, cyanide means CN replaces Br, but concentrated ethanolic hydroxide means HBr is removed.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{aqueous NaOH} \rightarrow \text{substitution to alcohol, ethanolic NaOH} \rightarrow \text{elimination to alkene}$$

**Write the four organic products**

Let's list what you actually make in each case.

$$\text{A: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Br}^-$$
$$\text{B: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Br}^-$$
$$\text{C: CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \text{Br}^-$$
$$\text{D: CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Compare relative molecular masses**

Now calculate Mr for each organic product by adding atomic masses.

$$M_r(\text{ethanol}) = 46, \quad M_r(\text{propanenitrile}) = 55$$
$$M_r(\text{propan-2-ol}) = 60, \quad M_r(\text{propene}) = 42$$

**Pick the lowest**

Elimination removes atoms so it gives a lighter product than substitution which adds atoms. Propene at 42 is clearly the lightest of the four.

options.A: Aqueous NaOH causes nucleophilic substitution to give ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Its Mr is 46, which is low but still heavier than the alkene formed by elimination.
options.B: Cyanide causes substitution to give propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$. A whole carbon and nitrogen are added, so Mr rises to 55, the second highest here.
options.C: Aqueous NaOH with 2-bromopropane gives propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Its Mr is 60, the highest of the four because OH replaces Br on a 3-carbon chain.
options.D: Concentrated ethanolic NaOH causes elimination (dehydrohalogenation) to give propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$. No heavy group is added and HBr is lost, so Mr is only 42, the lowest of all four.
